data.narrative:
General Matter is a Series A nuclear energy company founded by Scott Nolan and Lee Robinson that has raised $50M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 11 frontier nuclear peers (3 public, 8 private), including Fuse Energy, X-Energy, Oklo, and Nano Nuclear Energy, though the private peer set lacks sufficient same-stage density for median-based triangulation.

Given the sparse comparable set in nuclear energy at General Matter's stage and valuation tier, only the stage-progression method is reliably applicable. Using total raised ($50M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A progression yields an implied valuation of $100M. This method assumes a normalized step pattern from total capital deployed to post-A valuation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $85M to $115M, with a median point of $100M. Key uncertainties include the appropriate step-up multiplier for frontier nuclear (stage-progression assumes 2.0x but nuclear's capital intensity and regulatory complexity may warrant calibration), the representativeness of the limited peer universe, and General Matter's specific asset maturity relative to comparable companies. A fuller peer-median approach remains constrained by the absence of at least three meaningfully comparable Series A nuclear-energy companies with disclosed valuations.
